survivingClaim: For a cubic-theta row T = L0 D with L0(s) = L(3s - 1/2, psi) (imprimitive at the bad primes), the row's reflection axis Re s = 1/2 is Re w = 1 for L0, 1/6 from L0's own axis Re s = 1/3; the reflection quotient of T about its axis has no pole from a zero of L0 (classical non-vanishing on Re w >= 1). For the unweighted row eta = 1, m = 1, mask at 2 (T has a simple pole at 5/6, confirmed by a parameter-free test, and no pole at 1/6), a float64 fit gives T(s_rho) != 0 at eight low zeros of zeta_F (one, 18.262, with margin about 4), so D has poles there; where T(s_rho) != 0 the reflected pole of D has real part (5/2 - beta)/3, which restates beta and carries no sign or rank condition. About Re s = 1/3 the non-trivial zeros of L0 cancel from the reflection quotient of D and the log-derivative form is H(T) - H(L0) with no sign from the row's functional equation. This is the classical Kubota-Patterson normalisation in bridge language: an obstruction record, not a new theorem. Not established: T(s_rho) != 0 for any twisted or weighted row; non-existence of a continuation for THIN; the Mellin form of the unrefereed manuscript's Prop. 5.1.
obstruction: A cubic-theta row is T = L0 D with L0(s) = L(3s - 1/2, psi). The row's reflection axis Re s = 1/2 is Re w = 1 for L0, at distance 1/6 (in s) from L0's own axis Re s = 1/3. The reflection quotient of T about its axis has no pole from a zero of L0 (classical non-vanishing on Re w >= 1); where T(s_rho) != 0 (float fit at eight low zeros, one unweighted row) the zero is a pole of D with reflected real part (5/2 - beta)/3, which restates beta with no sign or rank condition. About Re s = 1/3 the form is H(T) - H(L0) with no sign from the row's functional equation. The target L(s, eta) enters a single row only as a coefficient twist; it appears as an L-function only after the sum over rows. Classical Kubota-Patterson normalisation in bridge language.

lesson: A theta or Eisenstein-type row carries its Euler factor at the edge: its unitary axis is Re w = 1 for the L-function in its coefficients, 1/6 (in s) from that L-function's critical line. Bridges built on single rows land on the right-of-1 side of the R4 wall (Langlands-Shahidi / Sarnak setting). The target L(s, eta) appears only after the sum over rows, never inside one row.
